claim: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(Q=x^2+yz\), \(Q'=x^2+yz+y^2\), and \(C=y^3+z(x^2+yz)\), and let \(B=Q(Q')^2\). For the marked plane presentation of Zanardini's index-two Halphen pencil in Example 7.46, the subgroup of \(\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb C)\) preserving the sextic divisor \(B=Q+2Q'\) and the cubic divisor \(C\) individually is exactly \[\{1,\iota\},\qquad \iota[x:y:z]=[-x:y:z],\]hence is cyclic of order two. Equivalently, the projective stabilizer of the distinguished \(III^*\) fiber and the multiple cubic in this marked plane model is \(C_2\).
integrity: All algebraic identities used in the proof are exact. The source equations and bibliographic date/classification were checked against the public source. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The calculation determines only the projective stabilizer of the marked plane pair (B,C), not the full automorphism group of the resolved surface and not an unmarked pencil stabilizer that may permute fibers.
title: Projective stabilizer of the marked double-conic Halphen presentation
